Meeting header:
Date: 2026-05-12
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 40 minutes
Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Cho (Redwood SE), Jared Cole (Fallbrook - Head of MLOps), Maya Singh (Fallbrook - Platform Eng), Liam O'Connor (Fallbrook - Procurement)

Discussed latency/cost tradeoffs, private VPC vs dedicated hosted, SOC2 and audit logs. Next steps set for pricing and benchmark.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samira: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Samira from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account, with Ethan our SE. How are you all?
[00:06] Jared: Hey Samira, hi Ethan, thanks. Quick morning for us.
[00:09] Maya: Morning, yeah, thanks for fitting us in.
[00:12] Samira: Awesome. So agenda today, quick health check, renewal conversation, expansion asks — EU region and capacity bump — then we'll run through what Redwood needs to move fast. Sound good?
[00:22] Jared: Sounds great. We've been pretty happy overall, but obviously cost has been creeping up with the new inference workloads.
[00:28] Ethan: Totally, we saw that in the telemet— uh, token level dashboards you sent. We wanted to make sure we understood the mix of short chat vs long completion workloads.
[00:36] Maya: Right, majority is short prompts but we have a non-trivial tail of longer generation for doc summarization. Peak seq lengths around 4k for some jobs.
[00:45] Samira: Helpful — that matters for kernel selection and batching. Quick qual: are you leaning Hosted API + Dedicated pools or thinking Private/VPC?
[00:53] Jared: For now Dedicated pools are preferred. We like Redwood Dedicated for isolation. The ask is we need an additional EU region and roughly 2x current committed GPU capacity during peak. Also procurement is pushing for a 12-month extension if we can get price stability.
[01:08] Liam: Yep, procurement would like price protection and some uptime SLA guarantees baked into the contract.
[01:13] Samira: Understood. We can do a dedicated EU pool and an extension. For SLA — our Dedicated offering has SLA-backed latency and uptime tiers; we can map that to a package. I'll send terms.
[01:24] Ethan: On the performance side, two questions: what GPUs are you currently targeting in Dedicated? Are you seeing large variance in seq length distributions?
[01:32] Maya: We're on mixed instances today — some T4/RTX on prem for dev, hosted has been on A100 shared before. For Dedicated we'd like A100 class or H100 eventually. Seq distribution: 80% sub-512, 15% 512-2k, 5% 2k-8k.
[01:46] Ethan: That distribution suggests batching + KV cache will help with the short prompts and tails will need memory-forward kernels. We'll run a benchmark with an 8k profile to show performance impact and cost delta between A100/80GB vs A100/40GB and quantized runs.
[02:00] Jared: That would be great, especially if you can show unit cost improvements with quantization. We're a bit wary of quality regressions.
[02:07] Ethan: Totally, we'll include quality checks — a small eval set and rouge/semantic scoring.
[02:12] Maya: On the privacy side, we need VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, and audit logs per our security team.
[02:19] Samira: Those are standard on Private, and many of the items are also available on Dedicated as add-ons — KMS, SAML, audit logging. We have SOC2 docs we can share.
[02:28] Liam: Can you send those security docs and a network diagram that shows peering and firewall requirements? Procurement needs to sign off.
[02:34] Samira: Yes, I'll attach the SOC2 report, sample network diagram, and a compliance checklist.
[02:38] Jared: Also curious about burst capacity — our traffic spikes intermittently. Can Dedicated burst to hosted capacity?
[02:45] Ethan: We have configurable burst policies; Dedicated can be configured with burst to our shared pool subject to policy and pricing. For hard SLOs we recommend reserved burst lanes as part of the commitment.
[02:57] Maya: If we add EU region, how is data residency handled? We need data at rest to be stored in region and logs to respect residency.
[03:06] Samira: We can pin model routing by region and have logs and storage per-region. For Private deployments it's customer-controlled. For Dedicated we can guarantee region-local storage and with contractual terms for residency.
[03:18] Liam: Great. Pricing question: what's the delta for adding a third region and doubling capacity?
[03:24] Samira: I'll prepare a concrete quote but high level you should expect a ~25-30% uplift for the extra region due to reserved capacity footprint, and another ~60% for the extra GPUs depending on instance class and quantization profile. We can offset with a 12-month extension discount.
[03:40] Jared: Okay that math seems plausible. Can you model options: A) 12-month extension with price protect + 3-region Dedicated A100 80GB; B) 12-month extension with A100 40GB + aggressive quantization; C) Private/VPC pilot for EU first.
[03:55] Ethan: On (B) we'll show perf delta; often quantization gives 1.8-2.5x token cost reduction but you need to check QoQ quality. We'll include sample evals.
[04:06] Maya: For (C) if we run a Private pilot, what's the lead time for on-prem or VPC private control plane?
[04:13] Samira: For VPC-private control plane in a cloud region it's typically 4–6 weeks for initial setup and networking approvals; on-prem air-gapped is longer and requires professional services.
[04:24] Jared: Timeline: procurement wants renewal signed by end of June to avoid price increases. Is that doable?
[04:30] Liam: We also need legal to review the contract — can you include our standard data addendum?
[04:35] Samira: Yes, addendum is fine. We'll share a term sheet with the extension and the addendum.
[04:40] Ethan: For the benchmark, can you confirm sample payloads — we'd prefer to use obfuscated production traces. Maya, can you share an anonymized trace and a representative eval set?
[04:51] Maya: Yes I can share that after a quick scrub. We'll strip PII. Expect to upload by Friday.
[04:56] Ethan: Great. We'll provision a test job and run A100 80GB baseline, A100 40GB quantized, and the Dedicated pooling behavior with batching. We'll output latency p95, token cost, and semantic eval.
[05:09] Jared: If the quantized path shows acceptable quality, we'd push more workloads there.
[05:13] Samira: Noted. Any blockers from your side?
[05:16] Liam: Procurement needs the pricing and the security docs to start redlines. After that legal will give us standard turnaround.
[05:22] Samira: Okay recap of next steps: I'll send pricing + term sheet + SOC2 + network diagram. Ethan will schedule benchmarks once you send the traces. Maya to share infra diagram and traces. Liam to confirm procurement timeline.
[05:35] Maya: Sounds good. Also, one small ask — can Redwood support RBAC integration with our existing SSO (Okta)? We need role-based access for dev vs ops.
[05:45] Ethan: Yes, SAML/Okta integration is supported; RBAC mapping is configurable. We'll include docs.
[05:51] Jared: One more question — are there any competitors we should be aware of with better pricing on A100s? We've been pinged by CloudAI and ModelServe.
[05:59] Samira: Heard of those; CloudAI often competes on raw price but lacks the production observability and rollout tooling we provide. ModelServe has an open kit but requires a lot of ops. We'll include a short competitive note.
[06:12] Liam: OK, that helps procurement to justify.
[06:15] Samira: Anything else?
[06:17] Maya: No, that's it.
[06:19] Samira: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the pricing and docs by Friday.
[06:24] Jared: Thanks Samira, Ethan.
[06:26] Ethan: Thanks all.
[06:28] Liam: Thanks.

(End of call)

Notes on transcript quality: automated transcription had a few mis-hearings ("KV cash" for KV cache, "V P C" sometimes split, some names slightly off). Speaker labels are accurate but occasional overlaps.
